intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-14 (HMND14) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding the largest subunit of dynactin (DCTN1) on chromosome 2p13.

checks.claim: Distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-14 (HMND14) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the DCTN1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutation analysis of a gene in this interval that encodes the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin showed a single base-pair change resulting in an amino-acid substitution
checks.explanation: The abstract links a lower motor neuron disease to a mutation in the dynactin gene. It does not state that the mutation is heterozygous, does not use the name HMND14 and does not give the inheritance pattern. Only the abstract was supplied, so these details may appear in the full text.

checks.claim: The DCTN1 gene encodes the largest subunit of dynactin.
checks.evidence_quote: a gene in this interval that encodes the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin
checks.explanation: The abstract says this directly; DCTN1 is the standard symbol for this gene.

checks.claim: The DCTN1 gene is located on chromosome 2p13.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we show linkage of a lower motor neuron disease to a region of 4 Mb at chromosome 2p13. Mutation analysis of a gene in this interval
checks.explanation: The dynactin gene lies in the linked interval at chromosome 2p13.

paragraphs.text: Distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-14 is a lower motor neuron disease. Puls et al. (2003) showed that it is caused by mutation in the gene encoding the largest subunit of dynactin, a protein involved in axonal transport.

checks.claim: Distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-14 is a lower motor neuron disease.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we show linkage of a lower motor neuron disease to a region of 4 Mb at chromosome 2p13.
checks.explanation: The paper describes the disease as a lower motor neuron disease. HMND14 is the draft's own nomenclature for it.

checks.claim: Puls et al. (2003) showed that distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-14 is caused by mutation in the gene encoding the largest subunit of dynactin.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutation analysis of a gene in this interval that encodes the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin showed a single base-pair change resulting in an amino-acid substitution
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a causal mutation in the gene for the largest dynactin subunit.

checks.claim: Dynactin is a protein involved in axonal transport.
checks.evidence_quote: the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin
checks.explanation: The abstract calls dynactin an axonal transport protein.

paragraphs.text: Puls et al. (2003) linked a lower motor neuron disease to a 4-Mb region on chromosome 2p13.

checks.claim: Puls et al. (2003) linked a lower motor neuron disease to a 4-Mb region on chromosome 2p13.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we show linkage of a lower motor neuron disease to a region of 4 Mb at chromosome 2p13.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Puls et al. (2003) screened a gene in the 2p13 linkage interval that encodes the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin in a family with lower motor neuron disease. They found a single base-pair change causing an amino acid substitution that was predicted to distort the folding of the dynactin microtubule-binding domain. In binding assays, the mutant protein bound microtubules less well than normal. Puls et al. (2003) concluded that dysfunction of dynactin-mediated transport can cause human motor neuron disease.

checks.claim: Puls et al. (2003) screened a gene in the 2p13 linkage interval encoding the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin in a family with lower motor neuron disease.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutation analysis of a gene in this interval that encodes the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin
checks.explanation: The screening of the gene is supported, but the abstract does not say the study involved a single family; that detail may be in the full text, which was not supplied.

checks.claim: In the family with lower motor neuron disease, Puls et al. (2003) found a single base-pair change in the dynactin largest-subunit gene causing an amino acid substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: showed a single base-pair change resulting in an amino-acid substitution
checks.explanation: The single base-pair change and the resulting amino acid substitution are stated. The abstract does not mention a family.

checks.claim: The amino acid substitution found by Puls et al. (2003) in the dynactin largest subunit was predicted to distort the folding of the dynactin microtubule-binding domain.
checks.evidence_quote: an amino-acid substitution that is predicted to distort the folding of dynactin's microtubule-binding domain
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: In binding assays, the mutant dynactin subunit identified by Puls et al. (2003) bound microtubules less well than the normal protein.
checks.evidence_quote: Binding assays show decreased binding of the mutant protein to microtubules.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Puls et al. (2003) concluded that dysfunction of dynactin-mediated transport can cause human motor neuron disease.
checks.evidence_quote: Our results show that dysfunction of dynactin-mediated transport can lead to human motor neuron disease.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this conclusion directly.

paragraphs.text: Münch et al. (2004) screened the genes encoding the p150 subunit of dynactin (DCTN1) and the cytoplasmic dynein heavy chain (DNCHC1) in 250 patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and 150 unrelated control subjects. They found heterozygous missense mutations in DCTN1 in 1 apparently sporadic ALS patient (T1249I) and 1 person with familial ALS (M571T). They also found a third change (R785W) in 2 patients with familial ALS and in 2 unaffected relatives from the same kindred. Münch et al. (2004) suggested that these DCTN1 variants may be a previously unknown genomic risk factor for ALS.

paragraphs.text: Impaired axonal transport in motor neurons has been proposed as a mechanism of neuronal degeneration in motor neuron disease. Puls et al. (2003) found that a mutant dynactin subunit bound microtubules less well than normal. They concluded that this supports a role for impaired dynactin-mediated transport in human motor neuron disease.

checks.claim: Impaired axonal transport in motor neurons has been proposed as a mechanism of neuronal degeneration in motor neuron disease.
checks.evidence_quote: Impaired axonal transport in motor neurons has been proposed as a mechanism for neuronal degeneration in motor neuron disease.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Puls et al. (2003) found that a mutant dynactin subunit bound microtubules less well than normal.
checks.evidence_quote: Binding assays show decreased binding of the mutant protein to microtubules.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Puls et al. (2003) concluded that reduced microtubule binding by the mutant dynactin subunit supports a role for impaired dynactin-mediated transport in human motor neuron disease.
checks.evidence_quote: Binding assays show decreased binding of the mutant protein to microtubules. Our results show that dysfunction of dynactin-mediated transport can lead to human motor neuron disease.
checks.explanation: The conclusion follows from the results the abstract reports.
